newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada's RBC Dominion buys rival broker - sources.
newsitem.headline: Canada's RBC Dominion buys rival broker - sources.

text.p: RBC Dominion Securities Inc. on Thursday signed a C$480 million ($351.23 million U.S.) deal to buy broker Richardson Greenshields of Canada Ltd., a move which will catapult it back into top spot among Canadian brokerages.
"This merger has the full support of the senior management team at Richardson Greenshields," said George Richardson of the Richardson family, which holds 70 percent of the brokerage.
The merger will spell the demise of one of the last remaining independent brokerages in Canada.

Richardson Greenshields' loss of independence to Royal Bank of Canada, which controls RBC Dominion, is prompting speculation that more of the so-called independents will be snapped up in the near future.

A spokesman said the purchase, slated to close Nov. 1, will combine RBC Dominion's 1,020-strong sales force with Richardson Greenshields' 575 brokers. He said the buyout will be done at twice Richardson Greenshields' book value.

The merger is a continuation of a trend which has been under way since the 1980s, when the banks were permitted by the government to purchase brokerage houses, giving the country's six big banks enormous power in the financial industry.
Royal Bank is the largest of the Canadian banks, but its brokerage arm in 1994 was usurped as the biggest fish on Bay Street, heart of Toronto's financial community.
Speculation has been rampant that RBC Dominion would try to regain its position as the top brokerage.
The union is likely to cause some bloodletting because of likely duplication in research and administrative areas.
"I think there is going to be some blood on the tracks but I think people understand that there has to be some blood on the tracks," said a source within Richardson Greenshields.
"I think most people think that if we have to lose our independence, it's best that we lose it to a firm of DS's quality," he added.

Shares in Midland Walwyn Inc, the second-largest brokerage in Canada and the biggest independent, have been rising steadily since the rumors of the RBC Dominion-Richardson Greenshields merger began to circulate on the principle that one marriage often begets another.
Midland, with more than 1,000 brokers, is the largest of the independent brokers.

"I think Midland wants to decide whether it wants to put on lipstick or make itself look really ugly," Fred Ketchen, senior vice president and director of equity trading at another bank-owned firm, ScotiaMcLeod Inc., said in an interview.
The Richardson Greenshields source said: "I would say that there has been a lot of tires kicked over there in the last little while."
But he said Richardson Greenshields is a lower-cost performer.
